prose.hook: Madagascar is the world's fourth-largest island, sitting in the Indian Ocean east of Mozambique with no land borders to speak of. Ocean currents have isolated it from the nearby African continent long enough that roughly 90% of its plant and animal species exist nowhere else on Earth.
prose.physicalGeography: The island has a narrow coastal plain giving way to a high plateau and mountains through its center. It lies in the Indian Ocean off Southern Africa, east of Mozambique, along the Mozambique Channel.
prose.climate: Conditions vary by region: tropical along the coast, temperate inland, and arid in the south. The island is periodically hit by cyclones, drought, and locust infestations, though its volcanoes have not erupted in recorded history.
prose.economy: Madagascar is a low-income economy that is nonetheless rich in natural resources, including graphite, chromite, coal, bauxite, rare earth elements, and semiprecious stones, alongside fisheries and hydropower potential. It is a leading vanilla producer and exports garments, nickel, vanilla, cloves, and gold, with industries spanning textiles, food processing, cement, mining, and tourism. Extreme poverty remains widespread, and a return of political stability has helped growth, though the economy took a sharp tax revenue hit from COVID-19; it is also described as environmentally fragile.
prose.peopleAndCulture: Malagasy is the dominant official language, spoken by nearly the entire population, alongside French and some English. The population includes groups of Malayo-Indonesian descent such as the Merina and Betsileo, as well as Cotiers of mixed African, Malayo-Indonesian, and Arab ancestry, plus French, Indian, Creole, and Comoran communities. Christianity is the largest religious affiliation, split among several churches and Roman Catholicism, with smaller shares practicing traditional/animist beliefs or Islam, and a notable portion identifying with no religion.
